I work with local and international businesses, and I handle every account myself. Before budget is scaled, I check that your Meta Pixel and Conversions API are reporting the right events, so campaign decisions rest on data you can check.
What to expect
Campaigns built around your sales or lead goal

sections.title: Why Facebook and Instagram ads stop paying off

nodes.text: Meta ads rarely fail because of one setting. Usually several small problems add up: unclear goals, data the platform can't learn from, ads that have run too long, and a landing page that loses people after the click. If any of these sound familiar, an account review is a sensible first step.

nodes.title: Spend without a clear return
nodes.text: Budget goes out every day, but sales or inquiries rise and fall for no obvious reason. Boosted posts and broad audiences make it hard to see what is working.

nodes.title: Leads that don't become customers
nodes.text: Cheap form fills look good in Ads Manager, but your team spends hours chasing people who never intended to buy or book.

nodes.title: Ads that have stopped working
nodes.text: The same few ads run for months. Frequency climbs, click-through rate falls, and there is no plan for what to test next.

nodes.title: Tracking you can't rely on
nodes.text: Purchases or leads are missing or double-counted, so Meta optimizes toward the wrong people and reports don't match your actual sales.

sections.title: Talk to a Meta ads expert about your campaigns

nodes.text: Tell me what you sell, who you sell to and how your ads are set up today. If you already run campaigns, include your approximate monthly ad spend and what isn't working. I'll review it and reply with the opportunities I see.

I review your business, current ads and tracking.

faqs.q: What does a Meta ads expert do?
faqs.a: A Meta ads expert plans, runs and improves advertising on Facebook and Instagram so ad spend produces sales or leads. In my work that covers account audits, audience research, campaign setup, creative testing strategy, budget management, Pixel and Conversions API checks, and reporting.

faqs.q: Do you run Meta ads for both ecommerce and lead generation?
faqs.a: Yes. Ecommerce campaigns optimize for purchases and are judged on purchase value and cost per purchase. Lead generation campaigns optimize for form submissions, messages or calls and are judged on cost per lead and how many leads become customers. The setup, tracking and creative differ for each.

faqs.q: Is your management fee separate from the ad spend?
faqs.a: Yes. Your ad budget is paid directly to Meta through your own ad account. My management fee is a separate charge, which I quote after reviewing your account and goals.

faqs.q: How do you decide on an ad budget?
faqs.a: I base the starting budget on your average order or lead value, the cost per result you can afford, and the number of conversions Meta needs to optimize delivery. I recommend a figure after the account review rather than applying a fixed minimum.

faqs.q: What will you need from me to get started?
faqs.a: I need partner access to your ad account, Facebook Page, Instagram account and Pixel through your Meta business portfolio (Business Manager), plus website or store access if tracking needs work. I also need details of your offers, any existing creative and brand assets, and past results if you have them. The account, data and audiences stay yours.

faqs.q: Can you take over campaigns that are already running?
faqs.a: Yes. I start the way a Facebook ads consultant would: by auditing the existing account, tracking and creative before changing anything. That way campaigns that are working aren't reset unnecessarily, and changes are made in a deliberate order.

faqs.q: How do you measure Meta Ads results?
faqs.a: I measure results against your business goal: purchases, purchase value and return on ad spend for ecommerce, and leads, cost per lead and lead quality for lead generation. I compare Meta's figures with your store or CRM data, because Ads Manager does not capture every conversion.

faqs.q: How long before you can tell whether campaigns are working?
faqs.a: It depends on how quickly campaigns collect enough conversions to judge. Budget, cost per result, the length of your sales cycle, tracking quality and how much needs rebuilding all affect it, so I agree a review point with you at the start rather than promising a fixed date.

faqs.q: What does a Google Ads expert do?
faqs.a: A Google Ads expert plans, builds and manages campaigns so ad spend produces leads or sales. In my work that means keyword research, campaign setup, ad copy, conversion tracking checks, bid and budget management, search term reviews and regular reporting.

faqs.q: Should I use Search, Shopping or Performance Max?
faqs.a: It depends on what you sell and how much conversion data you have. Service businesses usually start with Search, which captures people looking for a specific service. Online stores often use Shopping or Performance Max built on a product feed. Performance Max works better once conversion tracking is reliable and there are enough conversions for it to learn from, and many accounts use more than one type with clear roles.

faqs.q: How much should I spend on Google Ads?
faqs.a: There is no single right budget; it depends on click costs in your market, how often visitors convert and how many conversions you need. I estimate click costs and likely volumes during keyword research and recommend a starting budget based on those numbers.

faqs.q: Is your management fee separate from the ad spend?
faqs.a: Yes. Your ad spend is paid directly to Google from your own Google Ads account. My management fee is a separate charge, which I quote after reviewing your account and goals.

faqs.q: What does a Google Ads audit include?
faqs.a: A Google Ads audit reviews account structure, search terms, negative keywords, conversion tracking, bid strategies, ads and assets, and the landing pages ads send people to. It's the same review a Google Ads consultant would do before changing anything, and you receive the findings in priority order before ongoing management begins.

faqs.q: What access do you need to my accounts?
faqs.a: I need access to your Google Ads account, and for ecommerce, your Merchant Center account. Access to GA4 and Google Tag Manager is needed if tracking has to be checked or changed. I work inside your own accounts, so the campaigns and data stay with you.

faqs.q: How do you measure Google Ads results?
faqs.a: I measure results by conversions and cost per conversion, plus conversion value and return on ad spend for ecommerce. For lead generation I also ask which inquiries became customers, because a cheap lead that never buys isn't a good result. I compare Google Ads figures with GA4 and your own sales or CRM data.

faqs.q: How long before you can tell whether Google Ads is working?
faqs.a: Search campaigns can start producing clicks and inquiries soon after launch, but judging performance takes enough conversions to compare. Budget, competition, conversion rate and the length of your sales cycle all affect how long that takes, so I agree a review point with you at the start instead of promising a fixed timeline.

sections.title: Why websites struggle to get found

nodes.text: Most sites don't have one big SEO problem. They have several small ones that add up.

nodes.title: Pages that target nothing
nodes.text: Service and product pages aren't built around the searches customers use, so they compete with each other or with nothing at all.

nodes.title: Technical issues in the way
nodes.text: Crawl errors, slow pages, duplicate URLs, wrong canonicals and missing structured data make a site harder for search engines to index and understand.

nodes.title: Content without a plan
nodes.text: Posts are published without keyword research or intent mapping, so they attract little relevant traffic and few inquiries.

nodes.title: Answers buried in the page
nodes.text: What you offer, where and for whom is hard to find in the copy, which makes pages less useful to searchers and harder for search engines and AI tools to summarize.

faqs.q: What do your SEO services include?
faqs.a: My SEO services cover technical SEO, keyword research and mapping, on-page optimization, local SEO and ecommerce SEO. Most projects start with an SEO audit, which sets the order of the work, followed by fixes, page improvements and monthly tracking in Search Console and GA4.

faqs.q: What is the difference between technical SEO and on-page SEO?
faqs.a: Technical SEO makes sure search engines can crawl, index and understand your site: speed, indexation, canonicals, redirects, sitemaps and structured data. On-page SEO improves what each page says and how it's organized: titles, headings, copy, internal links and how well the page answers the search.

faqs.q: How long does SEO take to show results?
faqs.a: There is no fixed timeline. Technical fixes can take effect once affected pages are recrawled, while ranking and traffic growth depend on competition, your site's history and how much content needs creating or improving. I report progress monthly so you can see the trend.

faqs.q: Do you offer local SEO?
faqs.a: Yes. For businesses that serve a specific city or region, I optimize your Google Business Profile, build or improve local landing pages and keep your business details consistent across listings.

faqs.q: Can you protect rankings during a website migration?
faqs.a: A careful migration reduces the risk of losing rankings, though no one can guarantee them. I map every important URL to its new location, set up 301 redirects, carry over metadata and monitor indexing after launch, which is how I handled GulKhan.pk's move from WordPress to Shopify.

faqs.q: Do you optimize content for AI search tools?

faqs.q: What does a Google Analytics consultant do?
faqs.a: A Google Analytics consultant plans, sets up and audits how a website's visits and conversions are measured. In my work that means GA4 and Google Tag Manager setup, conversion tracking for Google Ads and Meta, ecommerce tracking, dashboards and documentation.

faqs.q: Why don't GA4 and my ad platforms show the same numbers?
faqs.a: Each platform uses different attribution models, time windows and tracking methods, so some difference is normal. A clean setup removes gaps caused by broken or duplicate tracking, and I help you decide which figure to use for which decision.

faqs.q: What is server-side tracking, and do I need it?
faqs.a: Server-side tracking sends conversion events from a server you control rather than only from the visitor's browser, which makes them less affected by ad blockers and browser restrictions. It adds hosting cost and maintenance, so it suits businesses whose ad spend depends heavily on conversion data; many smaller sites are fine with Conversions API and enhanced conversions alone.

faqs.q: Can you track WhatsApp clicks, calls and form submissions?
faqs.a: Yes. WhatsApp clicks, call clicks, email clicks and form submissions can all be tracked as conversions in GA4 and sent to Google Ads and Meta.

faqs.q: Do I need Google Tag Manager?
faqs.a: For most sites, yes. Google Tag Manager keeps tracking in one place, makes changes quicker and safer, and avoids hard-coding scripts into the website.

faqs.q: How do you handle consent and privacy?
faqs.a: I can implement consent mode and a consent banner so tracking follows visitors' choices. Which rules apply depends on where your visitors are, so the legal requirements for your business should be confirmed with your own adviser.

faqs.q: Will tracking capture every conversion?
faqs.a: No. Ad blockers, consent choices, browser privacy features and cross-device journeys mean some conversions are never recorded. Good tracking reduces avoidable gaps and makes the data consistent enough to make decisions with.

faqs.q: What access do you need?
faqs.a: I need editor or admin access to GA4 and Google Tag Manager, access to Google Ads and your Meta business portfolio for conversion setup, and website or store admin access if code or plugin changes are needed.

nodes.text: I'm Umer Iftikhar, a conversion rate optimization specialist based in Karachi, Pakistan. My conversion rate optimization services help businesses get more inquiries and sales from the visitors they already have, by finding where people drop off and fixing what stops them.

faqs.q: What do conversion rate optimization services include?
faqs.a: Conversion rate optimization services find out why visitors don't inquire or buy, then fix the causes. My work covers a conversion audit, funnel analysis, behavior research with heatmaps and recordings, page and checkout recommendations, and testing or measurement of the changes.

faqs.q: What is a conversion rate audit?
faqs.a: A conversion rate audit reviews how visitors move through your site and where they leave. It covers analytics funnels, page speed, forms, product pages, checkout and the experience on mobile, and ends with a prioritized list of fixes.

faqs.q: How much traffic do I need for A/B testing?
faqs.a: A/B testing needs enough conversions for a difference between versions to be meaningful, which many smaller sites don't have. With lower traffic, I focus on research-led improvements and measure results before and after each change instead.

faqs.q: What is a good conversion rate?
faqs.a: There isn't one figure that applies to everyone; rates vary widely by industry, offer, price and traffic source. The most useful benchmark is your own current rate, and the goal is to improve from there.

faqs.q: Do you only work on landing pages?
faqs.a: No. I work on whole funnels: the message match between ad and landing page, forms, product pages, cart and checkout.

faqs.q: Do you work on Shopify stores?
faqs.a: Yes. Shopify conversion rate optimization covers product pages, collections, cart and checkout, within what your Shopify plan and theme allow.

faqs.q: How do you measure whether a change worked?
faqs.a: I record a baseline before anything changes, then compare conversion rate and the steps leading to it after the change. Where traffic allows, I run a split test so both versions are measured at the same time.

faqs.q: What access do you need?
faqs.a: I need access to GA4, permission to add Microsoft Clarity or Hotjar if they aren't already installed, and admin access to your website or Shopify store if I'm making changes directly.
